response.title: A Garden Through the Dry Weeks
response.passage: At the start of May, the science club planned a small garden behind the school. Because the water tank was old, the members worried there might be a shortage during the dry weeks. They agreed to cooperate: two students checked the soil each morning, while others collected rainwater. The caretaker was reliable; whenever the club needed tools, he arrived with the shed key. Before planting, Mei asked the club to reserve half the collected water for seedlings that had not sprouted. For three days, Ben observed the garden at lunch and wrote down which beds dried fastest. His notes showed that the sunny bed lost water sooner, so the club moved its new pots beside the wall. When a brief shower came, they filled the tank but kept the saved half for the seedlings as planned. By June, the seedlings were healthy, and the club chose the same plan for its next garden.
